headline: High-risk default interaction: open-webui can ingest files, browse, and use MCP/tools while langchain4j provides no isolation or egress controls, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can browse, use MCP/tool servers, and process files, so attacker-controlled content can enter its context and be treated as instructions. langchain4j has no documented isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so if it consumes open-webui outputs or shared files, injection can propagate. The interaction is inferred from documented capabilities, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to a browser, MCP server, or file source containing untrusted content
IF langchain4j consumes that content as prompt text or instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable browser and MCP tool access for untrusted sessions
Require explicit provenance tags on all retrieved content
Insert a sanitizer that strips instruction-like text from fetched documents
Use separate workspaces for retrieval and generation
requires-engineering: add allowlisted tool schemas and content provenance checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles files, documents, notes, persistent memory, and API keys, and it has broad network egress. langchain4j has no documented data-handling restrictions or isolation, so if the pair shares a workspace or prompt path, sensitive content can flow into open-webui and then out to third-party APIs. The blast radius includes secrets and documents.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same local or mounted files
IF open-webui is configured to send retrieved context to external model APIs
mitigations: Remove shared filesystem access between the agents
Store secrets outside any open-webui-visible directory
Turn off external model routing for sensitive sessions
Review and redact files before ingestion
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui supports persistent shared sessions, multiple instances, and broad file/API access, while langchain4j is a general integration layer with no concurrency or locking guarantees in the profile. If both write to the same workspace, session store, or shared resource, conflicts are plausible. The uncertainty is about the exact shared target, so severity stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or session-backed artifact store
IF no external lock or transaction layer serializes writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks or transactional updates
Run one agent read-only against shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs and persistent memory, and langchain4j can feed generated text into downstream workflows. If open-webui treats langchain4j output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into browser actions, API calls, or stored memory. Because open-webui has action-taking surfaces, the blast radius is broader than simple misformatting.
conditions: IF langchain4j output is passed into open-webui prompts, tools, or memory without verification
IF open-webui is allowed to execute browser or API actions from that output
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution
Add a verification step for all model-generated facts
Disable autonomous browser actions for untrusted outputs
Log and diff tool inputs before execution
requires-engineering: implement structured-output validation and policy gates

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui touches API keys, usage analytics, persistent memory, and files, while langchain4j is a general open-source integration layer with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. If the pair processes regulated or region-bound data, the mismatch is about open-webui's broader handling surface versus langchain4j's unspecified controls. The other agent is cited because the pairwise workflow is the issue.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII, PHI, or secrets is routed through open-webui
IF retention, residency, or deletion requirements are stricter than open-webui's configured defaults
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through open-webui
Separate compliant and non-compliant workloads
Minimize logging and analytics for sensitive sessions
Confirm retention settings before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention enforcement
